source: Mundler et al. (2025) Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models
finding: Decoding that enforces the type system cuts compile errors by more than half in synthesis and translation. Syntax-only constraining barely helps. Gain in functional correctness is small.
numbers: Models 2B-34B (Gemma 2 2B/9B/27B, DS Coder 33B, CodeLlama 34B, Qwen2.5 32B), HumanEval and MBPP in TypeScript. Compile errors cut 75.3% (HumanEval) and 52.1% (MBPP); syntax-only cut 9.0% and 4.9%. Functional correctness +3.5% to +5.5% relative. Syntax errors are only about 6% of TypeScript compile errors.
quote: reduces compilation errors by more than half and significantly increases functional correctness
limits: Open-weight models of 2024; not frontier. Needs decoder access, so it is not a prompt scaffold.
agent_relevance: Language design (types) is a hard constraint that the tool can enforce on the model. A type or schema check as a gate is cheap and helps. Answers gap 7 for constrained decoding.

finding: Type-constrained decoding helps most when the model must repair non-compiling code. Plain models often fail to find and fix the compile error from the message.
numbers: Repair: functionally correct fixes improved 37% relative on average. Vanilla Gemma 2 2B repaired only 33.5% (HumanEval) and 25.8% (MBPP) of non-compiling programs. Largest gains for small models (MBPP repair 11.6 to 20.9 for the 2B model); big models gain 1 to 9% relative on synthesis.
limits: Small models show the largest gains. 2024 open-weight models only.
agent_relevance: Bears on gap 5: error-message repair was weak for small models. No frontier-model number found. Use a compiler or type check as a gate in self-repair loops.

source: Cassano et al. (2022/2023) MultiPL-E: scalable multilingual code benchmark
finding: Codex pass@1 across 19 languages. Static type-checking has no overall effect on pass@1. Performance follows language frequency in training data, but some niche languages match popular ones.
numbers: HumanEval and MBPP translated into 18 more languages. Mixed-effects model, typed vs untyped, Codex: HumanEval typed x frequency interaction -0.36, z=-0.95, p=0.34 (main effect on type annotations p=0.33); MBPP typed -0.52, z=-1.2, p=0.23.
quote: Static type-checking neither helps nor hinders code generation model performance.
limits: Codex, CodeGen, InCoder only (2022). Languages differ in many ways beyond types, so typing is confounded with popularity.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 7 for 2022 models: language choice matters mostly via training frequency, not type discipline. Not tested on 2025-26 models.

source: Cassano et al. MultiPL-E type annotation ablations
finding: Removing Python type annotations did not change Codex accuracy. Replacing TypeScript types with Any lowered accuracy. Type errors in TypeScript output mostly mark real runtime errors.
numbers: Python without annotations: p=0.23 (no effect). TypeScript signature types all set to Any: -2.5% pass@1, p<0.001. Running TypeScript without type-check: no significant pass@1 difference (p=0.14).
limits: One model family, one benchmark (HumanEval). Small effect size.
agent_relevance: Types help the model only where types are the norm in the language. Do not expect a gain from adding annotations to a prompt in Python.

source: Shen and Tamkin (2026) How AI Impacts Skill Formation: main study
finding: Re-read the full paper. Developers learning the Trio async library with AI scored lower on the no-AI quiz; task time was not significantly faster.
numbers: Main study N=52 (26 per arm), pre-registered. Quiz d=0.738, p=0.010, 4.15 of 27 points (17%). With warm-up time as covariate d=0.725, p=0.016. Task time p=0.391. Pilot studies had 35% and 25% non-compliance in the no-AI arm.
limits: Single study, crowd-worker developers, one library, 35 minute limit. No replication found in this session.
agent_relevance: Confirms K02 and the corrections in critique item 2. Still single-source.

source: Shen and Tamkin (2026) six interaction patterns
finding: Quiz outcome depends on how the learner used AI. Asking for concepts, or asking for explanations with the code, kept learning. Pure delegation and AI debugging lost it.
numbers: Low scoring (below 40%): AI Delegation n=4, 39%, 19.5 min; Progressive AI Reliance n=4, 35%; Iterative AI Debugging n=4, 24%, 31 min. High scoring (65% and up): Generation-Then-Comprehension n=2, 86%, 24 min; Hybrid Code-Explanation n=3, 68%, 24 min; Conceptual Inquiry n=7, 65%, 22 min.
limits: Clusters of 2 to 7 people, post hoc, not randomized. Cannot separate the pattern from learner motivation.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: an explain-first scaffold is supported only by observational clusters, not by a randomized test in this paper. Gap stays open.

source: Shen and Tamkin (2026) closing remarks on learning modes
finding: The authors point to vendor learning modes (study mode, explanatory mode) as a possible fix but did not test them.
agent_relevance: No test of an explain-first scaffold exists in this source.

source: Lehmann, Cornelius and Sting (2025) AI Meets the Classroom: When Do LLMs Harm Learning?
finding: Two pre-registered lab experiments with Python novices found no significant overall effect of LLM access on learning. The effect depends on use: asking for solutions raises topic volume but lowers understanding; asking for explanations raises understanding.
numbers: Study 3 (replication of Study 2 with copy and paste enabled): 72 enrolled, 69 analysed, 78% no prior Python experience. Study 1 field data: 6,594 question-level observations in two graduate programming courses.
limits: Lab tasks short; exploratory use analyses are not randomized. Study 2 N not re-checked.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 3: a second source that agrees on a null overall effect and on the split by usage. Supports explain-first only as correlation.

finding: Low prior knowledge students learn less with LLM access; high prior knowledge students learn more. Students with LLM access overestimate how much they learned.
numbers: Reported from exploratory split by pre-test; exact coefficients not extracted.
agent_relevance: Matches K03 (gap widening). Adds an independent source.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Table 3 interface ablations
finding: Each interface part changes SWE-bench Lite resolve rate. Linting on edit, compact summarized search and a 100-line viewer window are best.
numbers: GPT-4 Turbo, SWE-bench Lite (300). Full SWE-agent 18.0%. No linting 15.0% (-3.0); no edit action 10.3% (-7.7). Search: summarized 18.0, no search 15.7, iterative 12.0. Viewer: 30 lines 14.3, 100 lines 18.0, full file 12.7. Context: last 5 observations 18.0, full history 15.0.
limits: One model, one run per cell; tokens and cost not equalised across ablations, so gap 9 (equal tokens) is not answered.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 partly: most harm comes from removing edit feedback and from verbose iterative search. Equal-token test still missing.

source: Prather et al. (2024) The Widening Gap, eye-tracking replication
finding: Replicated an earlier metacognition lab study with Copilot and eye tracking. Students who accelerated used suggestions well; struggling students kept known metacognitive difficulties and GenAI added new ones.
numbers: N=21 (earlier study N=31). 11 students showed no metacognitive difficulty. Acceptance rates: three accelerators about 30%, one 10% (2/20).
limits: Small N, authors state it. Copilot of 2023.
agent_relevance: Independent second source for K03. No test of newer models.

source: Kuittinen and Sajaniemi (2003) First results of an experiment on using roles of variables in teaching
finding: Five-week Pascal course, about 80 first-semester students split into three groups (traditional, roles, roles plus animation). Role teaching changed how students describe programs; effects on scores were mostly small.
numbers: About 80 students; groups checked with chi-squared tests for equal baseline. Program construction: roles and animation groups outperformed traditional, roles best. Comprehension: traditional and roles about equal, animation slightly worse.
limits: Same Finnish group as the method authors. Early report; not an outside replication. Nikula 2007 and other outside studies not opened.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open: no independent replication found. Effect on exam is small and mixed.

source: METR blog listing Dec 2025 to Nov 2026
finding: The blog listing shows no follow-up productivity RCT after the July 2025 study; later posts are about safety evaluations and risk reviews.
numbers: Listing from Dec 9 2025 to Nov 5 2026 scanned; zero posts on developer productivity.
limits: Absence on one listing page only; a follow-up could sit under Research or on arXiv. Not conclusive.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: no 2026 follow-up found. Treat K04 as unreplicated.
